tasks.title: Prop tip speed
tasks.statement: A propeller with a diameter of **{d} inches** spins at **{n} rpm**. Find the blade tip speed, m/s (1 inch = 0.0254 m).
tasks.solution: v = π · D · n, with D in meters and n in revolutions per second (rpm ÷ 60). For a 5" at 14,000 rpm: 0.399 m · 233 rev/s ≈ 93 m/s, about 335 km/h.

tasks.title: RPM from tip speed
tasks.statement: At what RPM (rpm) does the tip of a **{d}-inch** propeller move at **{v} m/s** (1 inch = 0.0254 m)?
tasks.solution: From v = π · D · n: n = v / (π · D) revolutions per second, multiplied by 60. For a 5" (0.127 m) a speed of 200 m/s is reached at about 30,000 rpm — the full-throttle RPM from the theory (course estimate).

tasks.title: Pack energy for transport
tasks.statement: LiPo **{s}S {c} mAh**, nominal 3.7 V per cell. Find the pack's energy in Wh (IATA uses it to decide whether the battery may go in carry-on baggage).
tasks.solution: Wh = Ah × nominal voltage: s × 3.7 V × c / 1000. 6S 1300 mAh — 28.9 Wh. Up to 100 Wh — carry-on without approval, 100–160 — no more than 2 with the airline's approval, more than 160 — cargo only (IATA 2026).

tasks.title: Charging power at 1C
tasks.statement: You charge **{n}** LiPo pack(s) **{s}S {c} mAh** in parallel at 1C per pack up to 4.2 V/cell. What power does the charger need at the end of the charge, W?
tasks.solution: The 1C current per pack is c/1000 A, on the board — n × c/1000 A. Power P = U × I = s × 4.2 V × n × c/1000. Six 6S 1300 — 196 W; if the charger is weaker, it will lower the current, and the charge will take more than an hour.

tasks.title: Energy of a spinning prop
tasks.statement: A prop with a diameter of **{d} inches** and a mass of **{m} g** spins at **{n} rpm**. Estimate its kinetic energy in the thin-rod model (I = m·D²/12), J. 1 inch = 0.0254 m.
tasks.solution: I = m · D² / 12 (m in kg, D in meters), ω = 2π · n / 60, E = ½ · I · ω². A 5" 4 g at 14,000 rpm — 5.8 J, at 30,000 — 26 J. The rod model overestimates the moment of inertia of a blade that tapers toward the tip, so this is an upper estimate.
